subject: Food Science
title: Vitamins and Minerals
description: A short lesson to help you apply Vitamins and Minerals.

hook.text: Your body needs 13 vitamins and at least 16 minerals. Miss just one and things go wrong fast.

buildup.text: Vitamin C prevents scurvy. Vitamin D builds bones. Iron carries oxygen. Each micronutrient has a specific job.

discovery.text: Boiling vegetables leaches water-soluble vitamins into the cooking water. Steaming preserves up to 90% more.

twist.text: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) need dietary fat to be absorbed. A fat-free salad wastes its own vitamins.

climax.text: Food fortification—adding nutrients to staples—eliminated goiter, rickets, and pellagra in developed countries.

punchline.text: Tiny amounts, enormous consequences. Micronutrients run the show.

quiz.question: Why should you eat fat with fat-soluble vitamins?
options: Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) need fat to be absorbed
